title: What does ISO 9001 clause 7.2 require for competence?
description: What ISO 9001 clause 7.2 requires for competence, how it links to awareness in 7.3, what auditors check, and what the September 2026 edition means.
shortAnswer: ISO 9001 clause 7.2 requires an organization to determine the competence needed by people whose work affects quality management system performance and product or service conformity, ensure they are competent through education, training or experience, take action to close gaps and evaluate whether that action worked, and retain documented evidence. ISO 9001:2026, published in September 2026, keeps competence in clause 7.2 within the harmonized structure.
keyTakeaways: Clause 7.2 has four parts: determine competence, ensure competence, act and evaluate effectiveness, and retain documented information as evidence.
Training is one way to achieve competence; mentoring, reassignment and recruitment are others.
ISO 9001:2026 was published on September 16, 2026; certification bodies report a three-year transition, with ISO 9001:2015 certificates expected to remain valid until September 30, 2029.
Certification bodies report that the 2026 edition extends clause 7.3 awareness to include quality culture and ethical behavior.
Auditors expect defined role competence and evidence of effectiveness, not only attendance records.
regulator: International Organization for Standardization (ISO), through accredited certification bodies
appliesTo: Organisations certified or seeking certification to ISO 9001
Suppliers whose customers or tenders require ISO 9001
Organisations using ISO 9001 as a quality governance reference

sections.heading: Which edition of ISO 9001 applies as at September 2026?

blocks.text: Both editions are in use during a transition. [ISO 9001:2026](https://www.iso.org/standard/9001) was published on September 16, 2026 and replaces ISO 9001:2015. Certification body [DQS reports](https://www.dqsglobal.com/en/explore/blog/iso-9001-2026-transition) a three-year transition, with ISO 9001:2015 certificates expected to remain valid until September 30, 2029, subject to rules set by Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (Global ACI, formerly the International Accreditation Forum).

For competence, the practical impact is limited. The 2026 edition follows ISO's harmonized structure for management system standards, in which clause 7.2 is competence and clause 7.3 is awareness. Published summaries from certification bodies do not describe substantive changes to clause 7.2, while [TÜV Rheinland reports](https://www.tuv.com/world/en/revision-iso-9001-2026.html) that awareness under clause 7.3 now includes quality culture and ethical behavior. Organizations should confirm clause wording against the purchased standard before updating procedures.

Clause 7.2 requires competence to be defined, achieved, verified and evidenced for everyone doing work under the organization's control that affects the performance and effectiveness of the quality management system (QMS). The summary below follows ISO 9001:2015, the edition most certificates are held against during the transition; certification body summaries of ISO 9001:2026 report no substantive change to it. In summary, the organization must:

items: determine the necessary competence of those persons
ensure those persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience
where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken
retain appropriate documented information as evidence of competence

blocks.text: The standard's note lists applicable actions such as providing training, mentoring or reassigning current employees, or hiring or contracting competent persons. This makes clause 7.2 an outcome requirement. A training course is only evidence of competence if the organization has defined what competence means for the role and checked that the person now meets it.

It covers persons doing work under the organization's control whose work affects QMS performance and effectiveness, which includes employees, contractors and outsourced personnel where the organization controls the work. It is not limited to quality staff: production operators, inspectors, customer service, designers, purchasing and managers can all affect conformity.

Clause 7.2 is linked to other parts of the standard. In ISO 9001:2015, clause 7.1.6 covers organizational knowledge, clause 7.3 covers awareness, and clause 8.4 covers control of externally provided processes, which can include supplier personnel competence. A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) or [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) is the usual tool for bringing these together.

sections.heading: How is clause 7.3 awareness different from competence?

blocks.text: Awareness is what everyone must know; competence is what specific roles must be able to do. Under ISO 9001:2015, clause 7.3 requires people doing work under the organization's control to be aware of the quality policy, relevant quality objectives, their contribution to QMS effectiveness including the benefits of improved performance, and the implications of not conforming.

Certification body summaries of ISO 9001:2026 report that awareness now extends to quality culture and ethical behavior. For training owners, that points to adding culture and ethics content to induction and refresher material, and being ready to show auditors that staff understand it.

sections.heading: What evidence do auditors expect for clause 7.2?

blocks.text: Auditors expect to see defined competence for roles, records showing each person meets it, and evaluation of any actions taken to close gaps. The table below is an illustrative model that satisfies each part of the clause.

blocks.caption: Illustrative mapping: clause 7.2 element to learning design to evidence
head: Clause 7.2 element
What to design
Evidence to retain
rows: Competence statements per role, drawn from process risks and product requirements
Approved role competence profiles with version and date
Assessment method for each competence, such as observation, practical test or verified qualification
Assessment records per person, qualifications, verified experience
Training, mentoring, reassignment or recruitment plan for each gap
Individual development plans and completion records
Re-assessment or performance measure after the action
Before and after results, supervisor sign off, defect or error trends
A single register linking people, roles, competences and evidence
Register export available for audit sampling

blocks.text: For step by step methods, see [how to build a competency framework](/guides/how-to-build-a-competency-framework), [how to conduct a training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis) and [how to measure training effectiveness](/guides/how-to-measure-training-effectiveness).

sections.heading: What are common audit findings against clause 7.2?

blocks.text: The most frequent weakness is equating attendance with competence. Other typical gaps follow from the same cause: competence has not been defined, so it cannot be verified.

items: Role descriptions list duties but not the competence needed to perform them.
Training records exist but there is no evaluation of whether the training worked.
Temporary staff and contractors are missing from the competence register.
Competence requirements are not revised when processes, products or the standard change.
Evidence is held in separate systems, so sampling during an audit is slow and incomplete.

blocks.text: The transition to ISO 9001:2026 is a natural point to fix these gaps, since procedures and training will be reviewed anyway. Related management system requirements work the same way in [ISO/IEC 27001](/regulations/iso-27001-awareness-training-requirements) and [ISO 45001](/regulations/iso-45001-competence-and-awareness).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines role competencies as structured concepts with assessment points before training content is written, so clause 7.2(a) is answered by design and 7.2(b) to (d) by recorded assessment evidence. The same competence definitions can be mapped to ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 45001 at once.

faqs.q: Does ISO 9001 require a training matrix?
faqs.a: No. ISO 9001 does not name a training matrix. It requires the organization to determine competence, ensure people are competent, act on gaps, evaluate effectiveness and retain evidence. A training or skills matrix is a common way to hold that evidence, but any method that meets clause 7.2 is acceptable.

faqs.q: Do we need to change our competence process for ISO 9001:2026?
faqs.a: Probably not in structure, since competence remains in clause 7.2 of the harmonized structure. Check the published text, and review awareness content, because certification bodies report that clause 7.3 now covers quality culture and ethical behavior. Plan the change within the transition period agreed with your certification body.

faqs.q: How do you evaluate training effectiveness for clause 7.2?
faqs.a: Compare performance against the defined competence before and after the action. Methods include practical assessment, observation by a supervisor, reduced errors or nonconformities in the person's work, and customer feedback. Satisfaction surveys alone do not show that competence was achieved.

faqs.q: Can experience count as competence without training?
faqs.a: Yes. Clause 7.2 allows competence on the basis of education, training or experience. Where experience is relied on, retain evidence such as verified employment history, work samples, or an assessment by a competent person against the role's defined competence.
